chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Maryam al-Ansari said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who said to a woman: 'Tomorrow I will come to you to seek your offspring,' and she will be free (of the waiting period/obligation) after he comes to her. Is it permissible for him to come to her and not ejaculate inside her? He said: 'When he comes to her, he has sought her offspring.'

key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: free/liberated (in context of marital status or waiting period)

ai.seo_question: Does a man need to ejaculate to fulfill the condition of 'seeking offspring' in marital relations according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the mere act of conjugal union (dakhul) fulfills the condition of 'seeking offspring' for the purpose of marital rights, even if ejaculation does not occur. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the physical act of intercourse and the specific biological outcome of conception, emphasizing that the marital bond is activated by entry rather than emission. It serves as a foundational principle in understanding the validity of marital relations in cases of infertility or temporary abstinence.
